ev.byz_m_baptism.text: You were baptized in the font, plunged three times right under. Your godparent, the anadochos, held you and renounced Satan on your behalf. From now on you are kin for life.
ev.byz_m_icon_lamp.text: An icon hangs in the corner of the house with a little oil lamp always burning before it. You learned to cross yourself before you could count to ten.
ev.byz_m_easter.text.1: Easter night: the church sinks into darkness, then hundreds of candles catch from a single flame and everyone sings "Christ is risen". You carried a tiny flame home, shielding it with your palm.
ev.byz_m_easter.text.2: After the Great Fast comes the Easter table: lamb, cheese and eggs dyed red. Neighbors kiss three times and answer one another, "Truly He is risen."
ev.byz_m_name_day.text: Today is the feast of the saint whose name you bear. Church in the morning, then guests, wine and everyone wishing you "many years".
ev.byz_m_psalter.text: The grammar teacher made you learn the first psalm by heart. You traced the letters with a stylus on a wax tablet, and every mistake earned a rap of the ruler across your fingers.
ev.byz_m_garos.text: You tasted garos for the first time, the fish sauce the Romans pour over everything. Visiting Latins wince at the smell, but you liked it.
ev.byz_m_resin_wine.text: Wine here is laced with resin and gypsum so it keeps on the road. A visiting Frank grimaced; you just shrugged. Real wine is supposed to taste like that.
ev.byz_m_hippodrome.text.1: Tens of thousands of throats roar for the Blues and the Greens in the Hippodrome. Chariots thunder past the bronze horses while the emperor watches from his box, the kathisma.
ev.byz_m_hippodrome.text.2: Between races, acrobats and a trained bear performed on the track. You shouted yourself hoarse and came home perfectly happy.
ev.byz_m_mese.text: On the Mese, the City's main street, the colonnades sell everything: Arabian incense, Rus furs, glass, spices and books. You walked from the Forum of Constantine to the Forum of Theodosius and were worn out by the smells alone.
ev.byz_m_hagia_sophia.text: You stepped into Hagia Sophia for the first time. The dome seems to hang from heaven on a golden chain of light, and even your chattering neighbors fell silent.
ev.byz_m_golden_horn.text: Venetian, Genoese and Pisan galleys ride at anchor in the Golden Horn. Each nation has its own wharf, its own quarter and its own church, as if the City had grown foreign fingers.
ev.byz_m_hodegetria.text: Every Tuesday the icon of the Virgin Hodegetria is carried out into the square, and people from all over the City follow it, hoping for a miracle.
ev.byz_m_earthquake.text: In the night the earth lurched, dishes crashed from the shelves and somewhere an old wall collapsed. In the morning everyone talked of omens and went to church.
ev.byz_m_rus_merchants.text: Rus merchants lodge by the monastery of Saint Mamas: fair-bearded men with furs, wax and honey. They may enter the City only through one gate, unarmed and no more than fifty at a time.
ev.byz_m_demetria.text: In October, for the feast of Saint Demetrios, a great fair spreads outside the walls of Thessalonica: tents, rows of cloth, livestock, Bulgarians, Italians, Armenians. The din drowns out your own voice.
ev.byz_m_myrrh.text: At the tomb of Saint Demetrios pilgrims are given fragrant myrrh. You anointed your forehead and smelled of roses until evening.
ev.byz_m_vlachs.text: In autumn the Vlach shepherds came down from the mountains with thousands of sheep. The town smells of wool and cheese, and the market women squabble over prices.
ev.byz_m_askania.text: You went fishing on Lake Askania beneath the walls of Nicaea. The water is as still as a bowl, and they say stones of ancient temples lie on the bottom.
ev.byz_m_olive_harvest.text: Olive harvest: the men beat the branches with poles while women and children gather the fruit from the ground. In the evening the press smells of fresh oil and weariness.
ev.byz_m_anchovy.text: In winter the anchovy shoals came into the bay, the little silver fish that feeds everyone here. People fry it, salt it and eat it with bread and onions, and the boats come back full.
ev.byz_m_sumela.text: You climbed the mountain path to the monastery of Sumela. Its cells cling to a sheer cliff like swallows' nests, and far below a river roars in the mist.
ev.byz_m_hazelnuts.text: On the slopes people gather hazelnuts and dry them on the flat roofs. You stuffed your pockets and spent the evening cracking them with a stone.
ev.byz_m_rain_pontus.text: Rain again, the ninth day running. Mist creeps down from the mountains, the roads have turned to mud, and the old folk say the sky over Constantinople must be a different sky altogether.
ev.byz_m_lent.text: The Great Fast: seven weeks without meat, cheese or eggs, and on the strictest days not even oil. Bread, olives and beans, and by the end everyone dreams of cheese.
ev.byz_m_panegyris.text: On August 15th, the Dormition, the village holds its panegyris: liturgy, then tables under the plane trees, music and dancing into the night.
ev.byz_m_wedding_crowns.text: At the neighbors' wedding the priest placed crowns on the heads of bride and groom, and they walked three times around the lectern. Then the whole street drank to the newlyweds.
ev.byz_m_fork.text: At dinner you were handed a golden two-pronged fork. Visiting Latins consider this Roman habit an outrageous refinement.
ev.byz_m_holy_fool.text: A holy fool in rags wanders the market, pelting the church doors with nuts and naming rich men's secret sins out loud. People laugh at him, and fear him.
ev.byz_m_digenis.text: By the hearth an old man sang of Digenis Akritas, the frontier hero who strangled lions bare-handed, beat the Saracens and wrestled Death himself almost to a draw.
ev.byz_m_kollyva.text: At a neighbor's memorial they handed out kollyva: boiled wheat with honey, nuts and pomegranate seeds. Everyone took a handful and said, "May God forgive him."
ev.byz_m_baths.text: The bathhouse is hot, crowded and loud. The attendant rubbed you down with oil, and the person on the next bench told you which dignitary was sent into exile yesterday.
ev.byz_m_slave_easter.text: At Easter the lady of the house gave each servant a new tunic and let them sit at the common table. One day a year you were almost like everyone else.
ev.byz_m_purple.text: No amount of money will buy imperial purple in the shops: these are the "forbidden" fabrics, woven for the court alone. But merchants will whisper and show you something almost purple, "for those who understand."
ev.byz_m_census.text: A tax assessor came with his helpers. They measured your plot, counted the oxen and the vines, and wrote down what you owe. Arguing with him is pointless.
ev.byz_m_tzykanion.text: On the palace field young noblemen play tzykanion, chasing a leather ball on horseback with long mallets. You knocked one of them out of the saddle. By accident, of course.
ev.byz_m_beacons.text: At night beacon fires blazed on the hills: Turks were near. The whole village, goats and bundles and all, crowded behind the fortress walls, and nobody slept until dawn.
ev.byz_m_old_hymns.text: You stand longer and longer in church, listening to hymns you have known since childhood. The boys serving at the altar used to get under your feet.
ev.byz_m_semantron.text: Before dawn a monk walks around the church striking a wooden board, the semantron, with a mallet. You have woken to that knocking for years.
ev.byz_m_eunuch_path.text: Your family has decided for you: you will follow the path of a eunuch. You will never have children of your own, but palace doors closed to bearded men will open for you. You will understand the price later.
ev.byz_f_pera_sabbath.text: On the Sabbath the Jewish quarter in Pera falls quiet: the shops are shut, and from the synagogue comes the reading of the Torah in Hebrew and in Greek. Your Roman neighbors joke that even the tanneries smell less that day.
ev.byz_f_romaniote_seder.text: The Passover seder among the Romaniotes: unleavened bread, bitter herbs and the story of the Exodus told in Greek, so that even the little ones understand.
ev.byz_f_imaret.text: A former church in Nicaea has become a mosque, and beside it stands an imaret, a free kitchen for the poor and for travelers. Lentil soup is handed out to everyone who comes.
ev.byz_f_pege.text: Outside the city walls, at Pege, the spring of the Life-giving Virgin, crowds jostle to wash in the holy water. On Ascension Day the emperor himself rides out there with his retinue.
ev.byz_f_orthodoxy_sunday.text: The Triumph of Orthodoxy: on the first Sunday of Lent icons are carried through the streets to remember the victory over the iconoclasts. You held a candle and listened to the hymns in praise of the holy images.
ev.byz_d_guild.title: Joining the Guild
ev.byz_d_guild.text: To open your own business you must join the guild. According to the Book of the Eparch, masters have to vouch for you, and there is an entry fee to pay.
ev.byz_d_guild.join: Join the guild and pay the fee
ev.byz_d_guild.unregistered: Work on the quiet, outside the guild
ev.byz_d_guild.unregistered.success: Customers turned up, and the Eparch's men noticed nothing.
ev.byz_d_guild.unregistered.failure: The guild masters reported you to the Eparch. A fine, disgrace and a shuttered shop.
ev.byz_x_guild_inspection.title: The Eparch's Inspection
ev.byz_x_guild_inspection.text: The Eparch's men have come to inspect: they check your weights, test your goods and ask whether you have been undercutting your fellow guildsmen.
ev.byz_x_guild_inspection.honest: Show them everything as it is
ev.byz_x_guild_inspection.honest.success: Your weights are true and your goods are sound. The guild warden praised you in front of everyone.
ev.byz_x_guild_inspection.honest.failure: They found a weight worn down by a hair. You had to pay a fine.
ev.byz_x_guild_inspection.bribe: Slip the inspector a couple of coins
ev.byz_x_guild_inspection.bribe.success: The inspector weighed the coins in his palm and left satisfied.
ev.byz_x_guild_inspection.bribe.failure: The inspector turned out to be honest. The fine was doubled, and the story spread through the guild.
ev.byz_d_eparch_price.title: Extra Profit
ev.byz_d_eparch_price.text: It is winter, goods are scarce and buyers would pay double. But the Eparch has fixed the price, and under his rulebook those who break it are flogged, shaved bald and expelled from the guild.
ev.byz_d_eparch_price.overcharge: Raise the price for trusted customers
ev.byz_d_eparch_price.overcharge.success: Nobody informed on you, and your purse grew heavier.
ev.byz_d_eparch_price.overcharge.failure: Someone informed. The lash, disgrace and a fine; for a long time you could not look your neighbors in the eye.
ev.byz_d_allelengyon.title: Someone Else's Taxes
ev.byz_d_allelengyon.text: A poor neighbor has abandoned his plot and gone who knows where. Under Emperor Basil's law, his unpaid taxes now fall on you, his rich and powerful neighbor.
ev.byz_d_allelengyon.complain.success: Your petition was actually read, and the collector reduced the sum. Unheard of.
ev.byz_d_allelengyon.complain.failure: The petition vanished into the chanceries, and you had to pay with penalties.
ev.byz_d_allelengyon.hide.success: The collector believed it had been a bad year.
ev.byz_d_allelengyon.hide.failure: The deception came to light. You paid three times over.
ev.byz_d_dynatos_land.title: A Magnate Buys Land
ev.byz_d_dynatos_land.text: The local magnate offers to buy your plot, generously, in silver. But then you will become his paroikos, working someone else's land and paying him. The law gives neighbors the first right to buy, but they have little money.
ev.byz_d_dynatos_land.refuse.success: The magnate shrugged and backed off. The land is still yours.
ev.byz_d_dynatos_land.refuse.failure: The magnate took offense: first his cattle trample your crops, then a lawsuit over the boundary begins.
ev.byz_d_dynatos_land.neighbors: Sell to the neighbors under their right of pre-emption
ev.byz_x_paroikos.title: A Paroikos
ev.byz_x_paroikos.text: For years you have worked land that was once your own. The magnate demands more and more labor, but in the bad year it was his granaries that kept you from starving.
ev.byz_x_paroikos.endure: Put up with it; everyone lives like this
ev.byz_x_paroikos.leave: Leave for the capital to find work
ev.byz_d_strateia.title: Military Obligation
ev.byz_d_strateia.text: Your family's land is listed on the theme's military rolls: the household must provide a stratiotes with horse and arms. You can serve yourself, or pay to be released.
ev.byz_d_strateia.sick.success: The clerk waved a hand and wrote down someone else.
ev.byz_d_strateia.sick.failure: The trick was discovered. A fine, and the whole village laughing.
ev.byz_d_pronoia.title: A Pronoia
ev.byz_d_pronoia.text: The emperor grants you a pronoia: the revenues of several villages in return for service with a band of horsemen. The peasants will pay their taxes to you instead of the treasury, for as long as you serve.
ev.byz_d_pronoia.decline: Decline; your own lands matter more
ev.byz_d_pilgrimage.title: Pilgrimage
ev.byz_d_pilgrimage.text: Your neighbors are setting off for Ephesus, to the tomb of Saint John the Theologian, where they say healing dust rises every year on his feast day. The road is long and not safe.
ev.byz_d_pilgrimage.candle: Send a candle and a coin with them
ev.byz_x_pilgrim.title: Memories of the Road
ev.byz_x_pilgrim.text: You often think back on your pilgrimage. One day a young neighbor comes to you: he wants to go to Ephesus too, and asks your advice.
ev.byz_x_pilgrim.help: Tell him everything and give him money for the road
ev.byz_d_novice.title: The Call of the Monastery
ev.byz_d_novice.text: The abbot of a nearby monastery has noticed how long you stand at the services and invites you to become a novice. The world and its cares can be left outside the gate, for good.
ev.byz_x_monk_doubt.title: Doubt in the Cell
ev.byz_x_monk_doubt.text: The years in the monastery pass in sameness: services, chores, fasting. One night you catch yourself missing the noise of the market and the smell of fried fish.
ev.byz_x_monk_doubt.elder: Seek the counsel of an elder
ev.byz_d_tonsure_old.title: The Tonsure in Old Age
ev.byz_d_tonsure_old.text: Many Romans take the monastic habit in old age, to atone for their sins while there is time. The monastery is ready to take you, with a gift or without.
ev.byz_d_tonsure_old.gift: Take the habit and make a gift
ev.byz_d_tonsure_old.simple: Take the habit, giving up part of your property
ev.byz_d_ktetor.title: The Founder
ev.byz_d_ktetor.text: You could build a monastery and become its ktetor, its founder. The monks will remember you at every service, and your portrait will be painted on the wall beside the saints.
ev.byz_d_ktetor.none: The living need the money more
ev.byz_x_ktetor.title: Your Monastery
ev.byz_x_ktetor.text: The monastery you founded has grown: it has vineyards, a mill and a hospital. But the bishop wants it under his control, and distant relatives demand the land back.
ev.byz_x_ktetor.typikon: Secure its independence in a founder's charter, a typikon
ev.byz_x_ktetor.typikon.success: The charter was confirmed. The monastery will stay as you intended.
ev.byz_x_ktetor.typikon.failure: The lawsuit drags on for years and eats up money.
ev.byz_d_demes.title: Blues or Greens
ev.byz_d_demes.text: Your friends want you to join the Blues. The Hippodrome factions are no longer street gangs as in Justinian's day but honored corporations with their own place in ceremonies. Still, passions at the races run as hot as ever.
ev.byz_d_demes.greens: Spite them all and join the Greens
ev.byz_x_deme_feud.title: A Brawl at the Hippodrome
ev.byz_x_deme_feud.text: After the races, at the Hippodrome gates, your fellow faction members have clashed with their rivals. Someone has already grabbed a club.
ev.byz_x_deme_feud.fight.success: The rivals backed off, and the tavern talked about you for a week.
ev.byz_x_deme_feud.fight.failure: You took a proper beating and spent a week laid up at home.
ev.byz_x_deme_feud.calm.success: They listened to you. It ended with bruises.
ev.byz_x_deme_feud.calm.failure: You got hit too, by both sides.
ev.byz_d_magnaura.title: The School at the Magnaura
ev.byz_d_magnaura.text: In the Magnaura hall of the palace, famous teachers lecture on grammar, rhetoric, philosophy and geometry. They take the gifted, and the treasury pays most of the cost.
ev.byz_x_sekreton.title: A Post in a Sekreton
ev.byz_x_sekreton.text: Your old teacher remembered you: one of the government bureaus needs someone who can write. The salary is modest, but the road upward is open.
ev.byz_d_buy_title.title: Buying a Title
ev.byz_d_buy_title.text: At court you can buy an honorary title, spatharokandidatos for instance. You pay a large sum up front, and then every Holy Week you receive a stipend, the roga, from the emperor's own hands, and a place in the ceremonies.
ev.byz_d_buy_title.no: Don't waste money on empty titles
ev.byz_x_roga.title: The Roga in Holy Week
ev.byz_x_roga.text: You stand in a long line of dignitaries in the palace hall. The emperor himself hands each one a bag of gold, while all around people whisper about titles, marriages and disgraces.
ev.byz_x_roga.petition.success: The logothete nodded: next year you will be raised a rank.
ev.byz_x_roga.petition.failure: They looked at you as if you had asked for the crown.
ev.byz_d_venetian.title: A Venetian Partner
ev.byz_d_venetian.text: A Venetian merchant suggests going halves on a ship of spices. Venetians pay no customs duties, so dealing with them pays, but if anything goes wrong, you will have to sue in their own court.
ev.byz_d_venetian.invest.success: The ship came back with pepper and cinnamon. The profits were split fairly.
ev.byz_d_venetian.invest.failure: The ship was "lost off Crete". The Venetian spreads his hands, and his court is on his side.
ev.byz_d_venetian.refuse: Have nothing to do with the Latins
ev.byz_x_venetian_return.title: An Old Partner
ev.byz_x_venetian_return.text: At the harbor that same Venetian hails you. He has grown older and richer and proposes a new venture: wax, furs and salt from the northern shores of the Black Sea.
ev.byz_x_venetian_return.join.success: The north proved generous. You grew rich.
ev.byz_x_venetian_return.join.failure: A storm off Cherson sank half the cargo.
ev.byz_x_venetian_return.refuse: You have had enough of Venetians
ev.byz_d_xenon.title: The Xenon
ev.byz_d_xenon.text: You have had a fever for three days. The monastery runs a hospital, a xenon, with physicians, clean beds and separate wards for men and women. Or you could go to the relics of Saints Kosmas and Damian, the healers who took no fee, and sleep in the church waiting for a cure in a dream.
ev.byz_d_xenon.xenon.success: The physicians bled you and dosed you with brews, and within a week you were on your feet.
ev.byz_d_xenon.xenon.failure: The treatment did not help. You came home weaker than before.
ev.byz_d_xenon.saints.success: You dreamed of two men in white, and by morning the fever had broken.
ev.byz_d_xenon.saints.failure: A night in the cold church only added a cough.
ev.byz_d_xenon.home.success: It passed; bed rest did the trick.
ev.byz_d_xenon.home.failure: The illness dragged on for a long time.
ev.byz_d_kommerkion.title: Customs at Abydos
ev.byz_d_kommerkion.text: At Abydos on the Hellespont the customs officers, the kommerkiarioi, take a tenth of every cargo. The captain whispers that he knows a cove where they can be dodged at night.
ev.byz_d_kommerkion.smuggle: Slip past the customs house at night
ev.byz_d_kommerkion.smuggle.success: The night was moonless and the cargo arrived whole.
ev.byz_d_kommerkion.smuggle.failure: A patrol ship caught you right by the shore. The cargo was confiscated.
ev.byz_d_kommerkion.bribe: Come to an arrangement with the officer
ev.byz_d_kommerkion.bribe.success: The officer recorded the cargo at half its size.
ev.byz_d_kommerkion.bribe.failure: The officer took the money, and the duty as well.
ev.byz_d_angareia.title: Forced Labor
ev.byz_d_angareia.text: An official has arrived: every man in the village must go and build a fortress wall and repair the road, unpaid and bringing his own bread. Only money or a special charter will get you out of it.
ev.byz_d_angareia.hide.success: The official left a few men short.
ev.byz_d_angareia.hide.failure: They found you. You had to work and pay a fine.
ev.byz_d_manumission.title: Manumission
ev.byz_d_manumission.text: Your master is gravely ill and thinking of his soul. The priest reminds him that freeing a slave is pleasing to God. You could raise the matter yourself, or wait for the will.
ev.byz_d_manumission.ask.success: Your master sent for a notary. Three days later you walked out of church a free person.
ev.byz_d_manumission.ask.failure: Your master turned his face to the wall. The matter was never raised again.
ev.byz_d_seventh_degree.title: Too Closely Related
ev.byz_d_seventh_degree.text: The matchmakers had agreed everything, but the priest, leafing through his records, shakes his head: bride and groom are related within the degrees where the Church forbids marriage. He will not crown them without the bishop's leave.
ev.byz_d_seventh_degree.bishop: Ask the bishop for a dispensation
ev.byz_d_seventh_degree.bishop.success: The bishop gave his leave, along with a donation for the church. The wedding was held in spring.
ev.byz_d_seventh_degree.bishop.failure: The bishop refused. The betrothal had to be broken off.
ev.byz_d_seventh_degree.other_priest.suc: A village priest married you without asking questions.
ev.byz_d_seventh_degree.other_priest.fai: The trick came out and the marriage was not recognized. The whole quarter talked.
ev.byz_d_relic.title: A Holy Relic, Cheap
ev.byz_d_relic.text: A wandering peddler unfolds a rag: "A finger of Saint Nicholas! A splinter of the True Cross! Yours for nothing." His eyes are honest; his supply of saints' fingers is suspiciously large.
ev.byz_d_relic.mock: Mock him in front of everyone
ev.byz_d_betrothal.title: The Betrothal
ev.byz_d_betrothal.text: Matchmakers have come for {npc}. By law a bride must be at least twelve and a groom fourteen, but the dowry and wedding gifts are being haggled over already, before a notary and witnesses.
ev.byz_d_tax_farm.title: Tax Farming
ev.byz_d_tax_farm.text: The treasury is farming out the collection of taxes in the district. Whoever pays up front collects from the peasants himself and, with luck, takes in twice as much.
ev.byz_d_tax_farm.bid.success: It was a good harvest year. You got your money back and more, though the villages curse your name.
ev.byz_d_tax_farm.bid.failure: Crop failure and runaway peasants. You collected less than you paid.
ev.byz_d_tax_farm.decline: Keep that sin off your soul
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.title: Pirates from Crete
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.text: The ship you were sailing on has been seized by Saracen pirates from Crete. Their island has a slave market, and captives come back from it only through ransom or an exchange of prisoners.
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.ransom: Wait for your family to ransom you
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.ransom.success: The whole family pooled the ransom. You are home, but poorer.
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.ransom.failure: The ransom did not arrive in time. You were sold at the market in Chandax.
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.escape.success: At night you jumped overboard near the coast and swam back to your own people.
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.escape.failure: You were caught and sold overseas.
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.work: Work off your ransom where you are
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.work.success: A year in someone else's vineyards, and they let you go home.
ev.byz_t_cretan_pirates.work.failure: The pirates' promises were worth nothing. You were sold.
ev.byz_x_exchange.title: Prisoner Exchange
ev.byz_x_exchange.text: At the river Lamos on the frontier, Romans and Saracens are exchanging prisoners, one for one, across a bridge. Your name was on the list. You are free again.
ev.byz_t_turk_raid.title: The Raid
ev.byz_t_turk_raid.text: A Turkish war band fell on the village at dawn. Those who could have fled to the hills; those who were caught are being led off to the markets of Konya.
ev.byz_t_turk_raid.hide: Run for the hills with whatever you can grab
ev.byz_t_turk_raid.fight.success: You beat them off; the raiders went looking for easier prey.
ev.byz_t_turk_raid.fight.failure: You were cut down and left for dead. The house was burned.
ev.byz_t_turk_raid.bargain.success: By handing over livestock and silver, you kept your life and your freedom.
ev.byz_t_turk_raid.bargain.failure: The leader took the silver, and you as well.
ev.byz_t_treasure.title: Buried Treasure
ev.byz_t_treasure.text: Digging a cellar, you struck a pot full of old gold coins bearing the faces of long-dead emperors. By law, treasure found on your own land is yours; on someone else's, it is split with the owner. But is this land really yours?
ev.byz_t_treasure.keep.success: Nobody found out. You changed the gold a little at a time, in different shops.
ev.byz_t_treasure.keep.failure: A neighbor informed. The hoard was taken and you were fined.
ev.byz_t_treasure.declare: Declare the find as the law says
ev.byz_t_accused.title: Denounced
ev.byz_t_accused.text: A neighbor has denounced you for reading the stars to learn when the emperor will die. Men are blinded or exiled for that, and the investigators are already knocking at the door.
ev.byz_t_accused.court.success: The witnesses contradicted each other, and the denunciation was ruled a slander.
ev.byz_t_accused.court.failure: You were found guilty. Your property was seized and you were sent into exile.
ev.byz_t_accused.bribe: Pay to have the case dropped
ev.byz_t_bride_show.title: The Bride Show
ev.byz_t_bride_show.text: Messengers have gone out from the palace: a bride is being sought for the young emperor, and the loveliest girls of good family are being brought to the capital to be viewed. Your name is on the list.
ev.byz_t_bride_show.go.success: Another girl was chosen as bride, but the dowager empress kept you at court in her own retinue.
ev.byz_t_bride_show.go.failure: You were politely sent home with a gift. Something to remember all your life.
ev.byz_t_bride_show.refuse.success: The messenger believed you and crossed you off.
ev.byz_t_bride_show.refuse.failure: The lie was discovered. The neighbors whisper that you think too highly of yourself.
ev.byz_t_inheritance.title: The Will
ev.byz_t_inheritance.text: A notary brings word: a distant, childless relative has died, and by his will you inherit a vineyard and a shop in a nearby town. The rest of the family is already sharpening its teeth.
ev.byz_t_inheritance.claim: Fight for the inheritance in court
ev.byz_t_inheritance.claim.success: The court upheld the will. The vineyard is yours.
ev.byz_t_inheritance.claim.failure: The lawsuit ate nearly everything, and one of the relatives became your enemy.
ev.byz_t_inheritance.sell: Sell everything at once to avoid a quarrel
ev.byz_t_groom.title: The Groom and the Nobleman
ev.byz_t_groom.text: You tamed a horse that the nobleman's grooms were afraid to approach. He noticed you and offers you a place in his retinue. They say Emperor Basil himself started out as a simple groom.
ev.byz_x_patron_fall.title: Disgrace
ev.byz_x_patron_fall.text: Your patron has fallen from favor: they say he will be tonsured and exiled to an island. His people are already being questioned.
ev.byz_x_patron_fall.loyal.success: The storm passed you by, and your loyalty was remembered.
ev.byz_x_patron_fall.loyal.failure: You were arrested along with him. You came out poor and sick.
ev.byz_t_fire.title: Fire in the Quarter
ev.byz_t_fire.text: In the night the warehouses by the harbor caught fire, and the wind drove the flames along the wooden galleries. Your quarter is burning.
ev.byz_t_fire.save.success: You got the most valuable things out before the roof came down.
ev.byz_t_fire.save.failure: Smoke and flames. You got out with burns and next to nothing.
ev.byz_t_fire.help: Fight the fire with everyone else
ev.byz_t_conspiracy.title: The Conspiracy
ev.byz_t_conspiracy.text: Friends in the senate invite you into a conspiracy: the emperor is weak, and they have their own candidate for the throne. Success means titles and lands; failure means blinding or the monastery.
ev.byz_t_conspiracy.join.success: The coup succeeded. The new emperor is generous to those who opened the gates for him.
ev.byz_t_conspiracy.join.failure: The plot was uncovered. You were forcibly tonsured and confined to a monastery on the Princes' Islands.
ev.byz_t_conspiracy.denounce.success: You were rewarded, but your former friends will never forget.
ev.byz_t_conspiracy.denounce.failure: Nobody believed you, and you yourself came under suspicion.
ev.byz_t_latin_suitor.title: A Latin Suitor
ev.byz_t_latin_suitor.text: A Frankish knight, one of the new masters of this land, asks for your hand. He is rich and courteous, but he is a Latin, and your relatives grumble that he is "one of those who sacked the City."
ev.byz_t_latin_suitor.marry: Marry him and keep your own faith
ev.byz_t_latin_suitor.marry_convert: Marry him and adopt the Latin rite
ev.byz_w_icon_commission.title: An Iconostasis Commission
ev.byz_w_icon_commission.text: A wealthy archon commissions icons for his new church: Christ, the Virgin and the Twelve Feasts. Two years of work, and the whole town will be watching how you do.
ev.byz_w_icon_commission.accept.success: When the icons were consecrated, people wept before the face of the Virgin. Everyone knows your name now.
ev.byz_w_icon_commission.accept.failure: The archon found fault with every face and paid less than he promised.
ev.byz_w_icon_commission.decline: Decline; you would never make the deadline
ev.byz_w_icon_workshop.title: A Workshop of Your Own
ev.byz_w_icon_workshop.text: Apprentices beg to study with you, and commissions are booked a year ahead. It is time to open your own workshop.
ev.byz_w_icon_workshop.open: Open a workshop and take apprentices
ev.byz_w_silk_purple.title: Forbidden Purple
ev.byz_w_silk_purple.text: Through a go-between, a foreign envoy offers to buy a length of purple silk, the "forbidden" kind woven only for the court. He will pay triple, but purple may not leave the empire: envoys have it confiscated at customs, and the weavers are dealt with harshly.
ev.byz_w_silk_purple.sell.success: The silk went overseas, and the silver stayed with you.
ev.byz_w_silk_purple.sell.failure: The cloth was found in the envoy's baggage. The trail led back to you.
ev.byz_w_silk_master.title: Your Own Loom
ev.byz_w_silk_master.text: Nobody in the workshop can set up the pattern loom as well as you. The guild warden suggests you buy the workshop from its aging owner.
ev.byz_w_silk_master.buy: Buy it with your own money
ev.byz_w_silk_master.decline: Stay a master at the loom
ev.byz_w_akrites_ambush.title: Ambush in the Pass
ev.byz_w_akrites_ambush.text: The lookouts report that an enemy band is coming back through the pass with loot and captives. There are few of you frontiersmen, but the mountains are on your side.
ev.byz_w_akrites_ambush.ambush.success: You freed the captives and shared out the loot. Someone will sing about this ambush.
ev.byz_w_akrites_ambush.ambush.failure: The enemy was too strong. You were carried out of the fight wounded.
ev.byz_w_akrites_ambush.signal: Light the beacon and wait for help
ev.byz_w_kentarch.title: Kentarch
ev.byz_w_kentarch.text: The general of the theme has seen you in action and offers you command of a hundred men.
ev.byz_w_great_race.title: The Great Race
ev.byz_w_great_race.text: Races for the City's birthday, May 11th. You bring your faction's four-horse team to the start, and the stands roar until the columns shake.
ev.byz_w_great_race.risky: Cut the turn tight around the post
ev.byz_w_great_race.risky.success: You passed them all on the last lap. The emperor tossed you a golden wreath.
ev.byz_w_great_race.risky.failure: The chariot overturned on the bend. You were carried off the track.
ev.byz_w_great_race.safe.success: Second place and unbroken bones. Not bad.
ev.byz_w_race_bribe.title: Hold Your Horses
ev.byz_w_race_bribe.text: Men from the rival faction offer you a purse of silver if you hold back your horses in the final race.
ev.byz_w_race_bribe.take.success: Nobody noticed anything except your purse.
ev.byz_w_race_bribe.take.failure: Your own side worked it out. You kept the money, but you were beaten and disgraced.
ev.byz_w_greek_fire.title: Fire on the Water
ev.byz_w_greek_fire.text: Enemy ships are bearing straight down on the dromon. The commander shouts, "Siphon ready!" You know that if the wind shifts, the fire will turn on your own side.
ev.byz_w_greek_fire.fire.success: The flames spread across the water, and the enemy ships went up one after another.
ev.byz_w_greek_fire.fire.failure: The wind threw the fire back. You were burned saving the siphon.
ev.byz_w_greek_fire.wait.success: The wind turned, and the fire went straight at the enemy.
ev.byz_w_greek_fire.wait.failure: While you waited, the enemy got its grappling hooks into the dromon.
ev.byz_w_fire_master.title: The Secret of the Fire
ev.byz_w_fire_master.text: You are summoned to the droungarios of the fleet: for your courage you are put in charge of the siphon crews of several ships. They still will not tell you what the fire is made of.
ev.byz_w_parakoimomenos.title: At the Bedchamber Door
ev.byz_w_parakoimomenos.text: The post of parakoimomenos is vacant: the man who sleeps at the door of the imperial bedchamber and knows every secret of the palace. There are several candidates, and all of them know how to smile.
ev.byz_w_parakoimomenos.seek.success: The emperor has entrusted you with the keys to his chambers. Generals now come to you with petitions.
ev.byz_w_parakoimomenos.seek.failure: Someone else got the post, and he will not forget that you were his rival.
ev.byz_w_scriptorium.title: The Scriptorium
ev.byz_w_scriptorium.text: The abbot has given you an old manuscript to copy: lives of the saints and the sermons of John Chrysostom. A whole winter's work by lamplight, until your eyes sting.
ev.byz_w_scriptorium.garden: Ask for a simpler task: the vegetable garden
ev.byz_w_hegumen.title: Electing an Abbot
ev.byz_w_hegumen.text: The old abbot has died, and the community gathers to choose a new one. Your name comes up more and more often.
ev.byz_w_forged_deed.title: A Backdated Deed
ev.byz_w_forged_deed.text: A distinguished client asks you to draw up a deed of sale with an earlier date, "so there is no confusion with the heirs." He pays generously, but a notary caught forging loses his post and is severely punished.
ev.byz_w_forged_deed.forge.success: The deed went through the court, and nobody suspected a thing.
ev.byz_w_forged_deed.forge.failure: The heirs hired another notary, and he found the forgery. You lost your post.
ev.byz_w_logothete.title: An Invitation to the Bureau
ev.byz_w_logothete.text: Your contracts are so flawless that word has reached the office of the logothete of the genikon, the tax bureau. They need someone who can count and not make mistakes.
ev.byz_w_village_priest.title: Parish Cares
ev.byz_w_village_priest.text: A bad harvest: for the feast your parishioners bring only a handful of grain each instead of their proper share. The bishop demands his due, and your own cupboard is bare.
ev.byz_j_icon_apprentice.title: The Icon Painter's Apprentice
ev.byz_j_icon_apprentice.text: An old icon painter saw you drawing saints on a wall in charcoal and offers to take you on. First years of grinding pigments and preparing panels; the holy faces come later.
ev.byz_j_akritai.title: To the Frontier
ev.byz_j_akritai.text: The eastern frontier needs akritai, guardians of the passes. The pay is land and freedom from taxes; the life is ambushes, pursuits and songs around the fire.
ev.byz_j_fleet.title: Joining the Fleet
ev.byz_j_fleet.text: The imperial fleet needs siphonarioi, men to work the bronze tubes of Greek fire on the dromons' bows. They take the strong and the tight-lipped.
ev.byz_j_charioteer.title: The Faction Stables
ev.byz_j_charioteer.text: The faction's head groom has seen how you handle horses and offers you a try as a charioteer in the morning races. Fame comes quickly in the Hippodrome, and so do broken bones.
ev.byz_j_palace.title: Palace Service
ev.byz_j_palace.text: The praipositos is taking young eunuchs into the palace chambers: to serve, attend and keep the seals. Many such boys, they say, went on to command armies and steer policy.
ev.byz_j_ordination.title: Ordination
ev.byz_j_ordination.text: The bishop needs a priest for a village parish: literate, sober and, if he means to marry, married before ordination. The parishioners themselves put your name forward.
ev.byz_j_ordination.stay: You do not feel the calling
ev.byz_mv_to_city.title: To the City
ev.byz_mv_to_city.text: They say there is work for everyone in Constantinople: building sites, harbors, workshops. A neighbor is packed for the road and wants you to come along.
ev.byz_mv_flee_ottomans.title: Across the Straits
ev.byz_mv_flee_ottomans.text: The Ottomans have cut the roads, the fields around Nicaea are burning, and no help comes from the capital. Many are already leaving across the Bosporus for Constantinople.
ev.byz_mv_to_nicaea.title: Escape to Nicaea
ev.byz_mv_to_nicaea.text: The City is in Latin hands. They say that in Nicaea Theodore Laskaris, the old emperor's son-in-law, is gathering the Romans and building a new state. Many have already sailed to join him.
ev.byz_mv_silk_road.title: The Silk Road
ev.byz_mv_silk_road.text: The roads to Tabriz are open, and caravans of silk and spices are coming down to Trebizond. Merchants say a fortune can be made there.
ev.byz_mv_to_thessalonica.title: To Saint Demetrios
ev.byz_mv_to_thessalonica.text: A childhood friend writes from Thessalonica: his workshop needs a hand, and the city is growing rich on the Balkan trade.
ev.byz_f_baptism_offer.title: Baptism?
ev.byz_f_baptism_offer.text: An official hints that if you accept baptism, the special tax will be forgiven and the guilds that bar Jews will open their doors. The community is watching you closely.
ev.byz_f_baptism_offer.keep: Keep the faith of your ancestors
ev.byz_f_hesychasm.title: The Light of Tabor
ev.byz_f_hesychasm.text: The monks of Athos teach the "prayer of the heart", the Jesus Prayer said with controlled breathing, and claim to see the uncreated light, as the apostles did on Mount Tabor. The learned Calabrian Barlaam mocks them as "navel-gazers", while Gregory Palamas rises to defend them.
ev.byz_f_hesychasm.palamas: Side with Palamas and pray the hesychast way
ev.byz_f_hesychasm.barlaam: Agree with Barlaam: God is known through reason
ev.byz_f_latin_neighbor.title: A Latin among Romans
ev.byz_f_latin_neighbor.text: You belong to the Latin community. Your Roman neighbors look askance: you take communion with unleavened bread, shave your beards and pray for the Roman pontiff. A neighbor kindly suggests you "become one of us" and join the Greek church.
ev.byz_f_ottoman_village.title: The Bey's Faith
ev.byz_f_ottoman_village.text: More and more villages around Nicaea are under the Ottoman bey. Those who accept Islam pay no poll tax and may serve the bey. A neighbor has already converted and urges you to follow.
